svg.title: The CloudFront request path, and where the cache key decides everything
svg.desc: A viewer request passes through AWS WAF, then the edge location cache, then a regional edge cache, then Origin Shield, then the origin. The cache key determines whether each caching layer can produce a hit; a cache key containing highly variable values such as User-Agent or a session cookie turns every layer into a pass-through. Origin Shield is billed per incremental request, and GET requests with a TTL below 3600 seconds are billed as dynamic.
svg.text: THE REQUEST PATH
Viewer request
AWS WAF
Inspects before anything is served or fetched.
Blocked requests never reach the cache or origin.
Edge location cache
Hit or miss is decided entirely by the cache key.
default key = distribution domain + URL path
Regional edge cache
Mid-tier. Consolidates requests for nearby viewers.
Origin Shield
Every layer's origin request funnels through here.
Duplicates collapse to as few as one origin request.
Origin
WHAT ACTUALLY DECIDES THE OUTCOME
The cache key governs every layer
Default: domain name and URL path only.
Query strings, headers and cookies are excluded
until a cache policy adds them.
Add User-Agent and you cache thousands of
copies. Add a session cookie and you cache one
copy per user — every layer above becomes a
pass-through, and the CDN stops being a CDN.
Need the value at the origin but not in the key?
That is what an origin request policy is for. It
forwards headers, cookies and query strings to
the origin without adding them to the cache key,
so analytics and telemetry values stop
fragmenting the cache.
The Origin Shield billing trap
Charges apply per request where Origin Shield is
an incremental layer. PUT, POST, PATCH and
DELETE always count — and so does any
GET or HEAD whose TTL is under 3,600 seconds.
TTL 300s → every miss billed as dynamic
AWS states Origin Shield is not a good fit for dynamic proxied content, low-cacheability content, or infrequently requested
content — which is exactly what a bloated cache key produces.
